flawed_step: The first substantive claim—triangle-freeness implies 4-colourability—cannot be justified. No proof steps were supplied in the input, and the explicit graph below is triangle-free but has chromatic number 5.
counterexample: Use indices modulo 5. Let H have vertices {a_i,b_i: i=0,1,2,3,4} ∪ {c}. Its edges are a_i a_{i+1}, b_i a_{i-1}, b_i a_{i+1}, and cb_i for every i. Now construct K with the 11 vertices of H, a distinct primed copy x' of every x∈V(H), and one additional vertex d, for 23 vertices total. Its edges are: (1) every edge xy of H; (2) x'y and y'x for every edge xy of H; and (3) dx' for every x∈V(H). This completely specifies a finite simple graph. It is triangle-free: H is the Mycielski graph of the triangle-free cycle C5; more directly, its displayed adjacency lists yield no triangle. In K, a triangle containing d would require an edge between two primed vertices, but there are none. A triangle with exactly one primed vertex x' and two unprimed vertices y,z would imply that xy,xz,yz are all edges of H, giving a triangle in H. A triangle of only unprimed vertices would already be a triangle in H. Thus K is triangle-free. To check its chromatic number, for any graph G the displayed Mycielski construction M(G) satisfies χ(M(G))=χ(G)+1. The upper bound follows by giving each copied vertex x' the colour of x and giving the new apex a fresh colour. For the lower bound, suppose M(G) has a k-colouring and rename the apex's colour k. Recolour each original vertex x having colour k with the colour of x'; leave all other original colours unchanged. Copies avoid colour k because they are adjacent to the apex, and for every edge xy this recolouring remains proper since x' is adjacent to y and y' is adjacent to x. Hence G would be (k−1)-colourable. Since χ(C5)=3, χ(H)=4 and χ(K)=5. Therefore K is an explicit triangle-free graph that is not 4-colourable.
assessment_summary: Proof attempt stopped at the universal implication after checking a concrete witness. Starting from C5 and applying the explicitly defined Mycielski construction twice produces a 23-vertex finite simple graph K. The triangle analysis proves K is triangle-free, while the colouring argument proves χ(K)=5, so the statement is false.
